messages:
ida: heads-up: exploring a "handoff sealing" layer between admission and coalescer to make lifecycle ownership explicit. thoughts?
raj: sounds like a good separation. three quick patterns: always-copy, pointer+epoch, or handshake reserve/finalize.
anya: tradeoffs: copy = safe p99, pointer = best p50 but GC tail risk, handshake = clearer ownership and telemetry but extra roundtrip.
ida: ops concern: any approach must keep low-cardinality metrics for SLA buckets only. per-tenant weight explosion will kill our dashboards.
raj: agree. also propose default policy: SLA -> copy, standard -> handshake, best-effort -> pointer opt-in. keeps paid customers safe.
anya: add small emit events: `handoff.event {id,kind,epoch?,hold_ms?,sla_bucket}` so traces stitch without high cardinality.
ops-bot: rollout suggestion: feature-flag handoff.sealing -> canary on 3 nodes; monitor p50/p95/p99 for sla bucket.
ida: action: i'll draft RFC blurb with lifecycle semantics and metric names. raj will bench pointer+epoch under GC stress. anya will sketch telemetry fields.
raj: will run microbench this week and post results.
anya: thanks. short and actionable. :thumbsup:
